findings.criterion: Eye protection and visible laboratory safety
findings.observed: Original JPG shows three unprotected laboratory faces. PNG shows transparent goggles on all three depictions; both front faces have wrap-around coverage and side/strap detail, and the profile observer has a visible lens and strap. The flame-test person now has eye protection. Coats, short hair and hands remain visually plausible. No fictitious claim of a complete safe execution protocol is made.

findings.criterion: Individual chemical labels and apparatus icons
findings.observed: Na+ next to a yellow flame is a plausible sodium-ion cue; Fe3+ charge notation is legible natively. Funnel/filter, mortar, balance and burette are recognizable method icons. The schematic apparatus is not a complete executable setup;15.2g and25mL are illustrative labels without a measured scale reading, concentration, uncertainty or completed analysis.

The recording actor stands to the notebook left and looks toward it; hand/pencil contact and turned pages are plausible cartoon perspective. Observer-facing headings are a normal infographic simplification. No mirrored person, reversed notebook operation or new goggle/hand artifact is visible.

findings.criterion: Depiction, age fit and style preservation
findings.observed: The friendly outlined comic style, blue/green panels, three preparation-analysis-documentation stages, sample handling and method symbols remain recognizable. The original is the actual existing style reference. No technical ID, provider watermark, copied worksheet or photographic style replacement is visible.

The three main stages and goggles are recognizable at360x201, but essential smaller chemical/result captions, superscripts, the quantitative detail and journal headings cannot be read reliably at that actual size. The densely packed text remains required to decode the specific illustrated chemical claims. Main workflow recognition alone does not meet the stated text-readability hard gate.
findings.requiredRemediation: Remove reading-dependent fine detail or substantially simplify the infographic so its required words and symbols are genuinely readable at360px; retain the three-step motif and correct goggles.

findings.observed: At680x380 the workflow, goggles, flame, most main method labels and endpoint jars are readable and recognizable. Journal microtext is still small. This better desktop view does not remove the observed360px limitation.

findings.criterion: Analytical conclusion represented by arrows and labels
findings.observed: The shared analysis panels show a sodium-ion flame-test cue, a positive-looking Fe3+ colour-test example, a mass label and a titration volume. Arrows lead to the unqualified endpoint identified pure substance: sodium chloride. No chloride-specific observation or expressly separate/conditional example routes are shown. A sodium cue alone does not establish chloride or pure NaCl; the Fe3+ example also is not marked as a different sample. This is a misleading specific conclusion in the image itself, even though individual method icons can be valid examples.
findings.inferenceBoundary: The scientific ion-test distinction is established; judging that this particular unqualified arrow layout can teach an unsupported conclusion is this machine visual review judgment. This is not an invented learner result.
findings.requiredRemediation: Use a limited, non-specific result such as documented findings/identification hypothesis, or explicitly distinguish complete supported example routes. Do not claim a specific identified compound from the shown evidence.
